handouts.read: They come at the wall at first light with everything, and the wall holds for about forty minutes.
players_know: This is the part the conventional plan accounted for.

handouts.title: Release, or Not
handouts.read: The decision point arrives earlier than anyone modelled, and it arrives while the line is still intact, which makes it harder rather than easier.
players_know: Waiting costs lives. Releasing might cost more.

handouts.title: The Loophole Test
handouts.read: If the Host is released, the gap in the contract gets tested in front of several thousand witnesses.
players_know: Whatever the safeguards were worth, you find out now.

handouts.title: In Motion
handouts.read: The battle does not pause for the argument. Both halves of it keep running.
players_know: Every round spent deciding is a round the line is holding without you.

handouts.title: Victory, or Retreat
handouts.read: It ends. How it ends is going to be described very differently by the Knights, by the city, and by the Conclave.
players_know: All three descriptions will be accurate.

handouts.title: The Demand
handouts.read: Kitiara uth Matar sends terms to Palanthas, in her own hand, naming one person and offering to leave the city alone.
players_know: The person named is not a surprise.

handouts.title: The Council Crisis
handouts.read: The Lord's Council has to decide whether a city is worth one man, and they are discussing it with the windows open.
players_know: It is closer than it should be.

handouts.title: Raistlin and Kitiara
handouts.read: They talk. It is a conversation between a brother and a sister and it is also a negotiation between two commanders, and neither of them drops either register.
players_know: Nobody else in the room is addressed at all.

handouts.title: The Sign
handouts.read: Something arrives with her army that the Knights' scouts will not describe in writing.
players_know: They will say the name once, quietly, and not again.

handouts.title: City Objectives
handouts.read: Four places in Palanthas matter tonight and you cannot be at all of them. The Council, the harbour, the Library, and the Tower.
players_know: Pick two. Properly.

handouts.title: Kitiara's Move
handouts.read: She is not going for the obvious one, and by the time that is clear she is most of the way there.
players_know: She has been in this city before.

handouts.title: Soth at the Threshold
handouts.read: He stops at a doorway he could walk through, and does not.
players_know: Something about this threshold is a question to him rather than an obstacle.

handouts.title: The Conversation
handouts.read: He will talk. At length, about oaths, and about what it costs to keep one past the point where it still means anything.
players_know: He is not stalling. He genuinely wants an answer.

handouts.title: Counterstroke
handouts.read: Whatever happens at the threshold, the rest of the assault does not stop, and something has to give at the other objective.
players_know: You will not hold both.

handouts.title: Safeguards
handouts.read: Every protection the party demanded is in place and documented, and the documentation is signed by people who will be held to it.
players_know: This is the most carefully prepared thing anyone in this room has ever done.

handouts.title: Memory
handouts.read: The Heart goes first. What it does is quiet and takes a long time, and partway through everyone realises it is working.
players_know: The room smells like Silvanesti.

handouts.title: Time
handouts.read: The Chronicle holds an hour open. Only one, and it is already running.
players_know: From here it cannot be paused.

handouts.title: Name
handouts.read: The Bell is struck, and it does not make a sound so much as make a space where a name should go.
players_know: Everyone present hears their own name for a moment, and then does not.

handouts.title: The Refusal Window
handouts.read: There is a gap — a few seconds, built in at the party's insistence — in which the soul being called can decline.
players_know: He does not decline.

handouts.title: Recognition
handouts.read: He knows his brother immediately and he knows the rest of you by name, which nobody expected and nobody can explain.
players_know: He is entirely himself.

handouts.title: The Sword
handouts.read: Caramon asks for his sword. He asks the way a man asks for his coat.
players_know: It is in the room. Somebody has to decide to hand it over.

handouts.title: Silence
handouts.read: Somebody says something ordinary and Caramon stops in the middle of what he is doing, and the room understands at the same moment.
players_know: The command channel is in him too.

handouts.title: Caramon Speaks
handouts.read: He works out what has just happened faster than anyone would like, and what he says about it is addressed to his brother.
players_know: He is not angry. That is considerably worse.

handouts.title: War News
handouts.read: A runner arrives in the middle of it, because the war has not been waiting.
players_know: Whatever this conversation was going to be, it is over now.

handouts.title: The Manifestation
handouts.read: He does not arrive. He is simply present, in the middle of the chamber, and has clearly been able to do this for some time.
players_know: Nothing warded against it, because nothing was designed to.

handouts.title: The Claim
handouts.read: He states that the research trail — the dead wizard, the laboratory, the missing record, the prepared gaps — was laid by him, for you, and that you followed it exactly as intended.
players_know: Check it against what you found. It holds.

handouts.title: Caramon Revealed
handouts.read: He says that the soul they called did not come from where they thought, and that he intercepted it on the way.
players_know: Caramon is in the room while this is said.

handouts.title: The Offer
handouts.read: What he wants is specific, limited, and far more reasonable than anything you were braced for. That is the technique.
players_know: He will not improve the offer. He says so.

handouts.title: Break
handouts.read: He leaves when he chooses to, mid-sentence, and the chamber is exactly as it was.
players_know: Nobody in the room can say how long he was there.

handouts.title: The Archive
handouts.read: Wayreth keeps its reasons. They are not written anywhere a person could read; the Tower simply opens them to you, one at a time, because the White Robe asked.
players_know: This has never been shown to anyone outside the Conclave.

handouts.title: Raistlin Recurs
handouts.read: In almost every future the Tower modelled, he is there. Not winning — present, at the point where the outcome turns.
players_know: That is why it chose him. Not because he is good.

handouts.title: The Blind Spot
handouts.read: There is a region of the Archive that is simply absent, and the Tower does not experience it as missing.
players_know: Everything that has gone wrong is inside the gap.

handouts.title: The White Robe's Question
handouts.read: She asks the Tower something nobody has thought to ask it, and the answer takes a long time to arrive.
players_know: It is the first time the Tower has hesitated.

handouts.title: The Accord
handouts.read: What the Tower understands by survival can be changed. Not overruled — changed, by agreement, and the agreement has to be unanimous.
players_know: You are party to it. So is he.

handouts.title: Two Maps
handouts.read: Both towers are attacked within the same hour, by forces that clearly coordinated it.
players_know: Wayreth and Palanthas. You cannot be at both.

handouts.title: Allocating Assets
handouts.read: People, artifacts and prepared magic, divided between two sieges, in front of the people being divided.
players_know: Whatever you send one way is not available the other.

handouts.title: Wayreth's Objective
handouts.read: The forest is holding and spending itself to do it. What it needs is time rather than soldiers.
players_know: It cannot ask for anything. It can only hold.

handouts.title: Palanthas's Objective
handouts.read: The city tower has the Portal in it, which makes it the real target and everyone knows it.
players_know: Losing it is worse than losing the city.

handouts.title: His Proposal
handouts.read: Raistlin offers a third allocation that is better than either of yours and requires accepting something none of you want to accept.
players_know: The arithmetic is correct. Check it anyway.

handouts.title: The Breach
handouts.read: Both walls go within a quarter of an hour of each other.
players_know: Neither breach was where the defenders expected.

handouts.title: Tower Choice
handouts.read: One of them can be held properly. The other can be held badly, or abandoned well.
players_know: There is no version where both are held properly.

handouts.title: The Portal Surges
handouts.read: With the city tower under attack, the Portal does something it has not done before, and it is not under anyone's control while it does it.
players_know: Whatever comes through now is not contracted.

handouts.title: Strategic Victory
handouts.read: It ends in something that will be called a victory, and the people calling it that will not have been here.
players_know: Count what is left before you agree with them.

handouts.title: The Decision
handouts.read: The Abyss expedition has been waiting while this happened, and the delay has had a cost that is now visible.
players_know: Going now is worse than going a month ago and better than going a month from now.

handouts.title: What He Remembers
handouts.read: A small room, a chair, and Caramon talking for the first time without his brother in the building.
players_know: He remembers everything, including the parts nobody wanted him to.

handouts.title: The Question
handouts.read: He asks whether he was brought back for his own sake or for somebody else's, and he asks it as a real question rather than an accusation.
players_know: He will accept an honest answer. Any honest answer.

handouts.title: What He Wants
handouts.read: It is smaller than you expected and it has nothing to do with the war.
players_know: Nobody has asked him this before.

handouts.title: The Ask
handouts.read: Then he asks you for something, directly, and it is the only thing he has asked anyone for since he came back.
players_know: It is within your power. That is why he is asking you.

handouts.title: Last Preparations
handouts.read: Everything that can be prepared has been. What is left is the part nobody can prepare for, and the party spends an hour not saying so.
players_know: Say anything that needs saying now.

handouts.title: The Crossing
handouts.read: The Portal opens properly for the first time, and going through it is not like any travel any of you have done.
players_know: You arrive together. That was not guaranteed.

handouts.title: Cutting the Line
handouts.read: The way back can be left open or cut. Leaving it open is an invitation and everyone can see what to.
players_know: Cutting it means finding another way out, and nobody has one.

handouts.title: First Threat
handouts.read: Something here notices you within minutes, and its interest is specific rather than general.
players_know: It knows what you are carrying.

handouts.title: Recognition
handouts.read: The field is full of things that were people. They have had their names taken, which here is a physical removal rather than a forgetting.
players_know: Some of them still try to introduce themselves.

handouts.title: The Name-Thief
handouts.read: Something here collects them, and it will attempt to take one from the party as a matter of routine.
players_know: Losing yours is not death. It is worse and it is reversible.

handouts.title: Use the Bell
handouts.read: The Bell can give a name back. It can do this a limited number of times and nobody knows the number.
players_know: Every use is a decision about who.

handouts.title: Caramon's Echo
handouts.read: Something in the field has a piece of Caramon that was taken on the way through, and it has been keeping it.
players_know: He is standing next to you while you find it.

handouts.title: The Mechanism
handouts.read: The palace is a machine for holding souls and it does not hide what it is. The workings are visible, labelled, and elegant.
players_know: It can be understood in an hour. That is deliberate.

handouts.title: Useful Power
handouts.read: What it does could be turned to something defensible. The thought arrives on its own, which is how you know the palace put it there.
players_know: The reasoning is sound. Check whose reasoning it is.

handouts.title: Redesign
handouts.read: It can be altered rather than destroyed, to hold fewer, or differently, or with consent.
players_know: Altering it leaves it standing.

handouts.title: Raistlin's Choice
handouts.read: He has an opinion and he states it, and for once it is not the one anybody expected.
players_know: He is arguing against his own interest. Work out why.

handouts.title: Break the Chains
handouts.read: Breaking it releases everything it holds at once, here, with you standing in it.
players_know: Most of them will not be grateful.

handouts.title: No Possession
handouts.read: Fistandantilus is here and he does not attempt to take anyone. He makes a point of it.
players_know: He wants something agreed to rather than taken.

handouts.title: The Offer
handouts.read: It is made to the whole party rather than to Raistlin, which is new, and it is made carefully.
players_know: He has adjusted it since Palanthas. He has been listening.

handouts.title: The Price
handouts.read: He states it without softening. It is not a soul and it is not a service, and it is worse than both.
players_know: He will not pretend it is small.

handouts.title: Caramon Answers
handouts.read: Caramon speaks before his brother does, and what he says is addressed to Fistandantilus directly.
players_know: He has worked out something nobody else in the party has.

handouts.title: The Argument
handouts.read: The party has the argument it has been avoiding since Arc III, in the Abyss, in front of both of them.
players_know: Have it properly. There is not another chance.

handouts.title: Break, or Accept
handouts.read: It comes down to a single decision and everyone present has to be party to it.
players_know: Both outcomes continue the campaign. Only one of them continues it with him.

handouts.title: Takhisis's Claim
handouts.read: She does not appear so much as become the thing you were already standing in. The claim she makes is older than any of the arguments you have been having.
players_know: She is not interested in the Portal. She is interested in who walks back through it.

handouts.title: Three Fronts
handouts.read: She presses on three at once: the war above, the thing in your party, and each of you individually.
players_know: All three are real. None is a feint.

handouts.title: Raistlin's Decision
handouts.read: Everything the campaign has been asking about him gets answered here, by him, in front of you.
players_know: Whatever he decides, he decided it some time ago.

handouts.title: The Dark One Ends
handouts.read: Fistandantilus's part finishes. How it finishes depends entirely on what was agreed in the last chamber.
players_know: He is not surprised by it either way.

handouts.title: The Portal
handouts.read: It can be closed behind you, or changed into something that is not a door.
players_know: Closing it strands anything still on this side.
Changing it has never been done.

handouts.title: Return
handouts.read: You come back to Krynn, with whatever you still have and whoever is still with you.
players_know: The war is still going on. It has been the whole time.
